# Schema ERD — auto-generated from the migrations, CI-gated against drift (MANDATORY for DB repos)

**The constraint (always-on):** every repo that **owns a relational schema** MUST commit a
**tbls-generated Mermaid ERD** under `docs/data-model/` **and** a `schema-erd-drift` CI job that
regenerates it from the migrations and **fails if the committed docs drifted**. The ERD is
reverse-engineered from the **same source of truth as production — the migrations** — never hand-drawn
(*"docs can't lie"*). This is the executable form of the SA **Data design / ERD** artefact
(`project-governance.md` #7) and a **Definition-of-Done gate** (same tier as tests + the as-built doc —
`agile-execution.md`, `documentation.md`).

The uniform standard for a DB repo is exactly three things (identical for all, no per-service variation):
1. `.tbls.yml` + the committed `docs/data-model/` baseline (or `backend/docs/data-model/` for a monorepo);
2. the `schema-erd-drift` **CI job** (the drift gate);
3. it **auto-appears** on the central ERD index (`minicloud-platform-docs` `gen-erd-index.py`) — nothing to do.

**The dbt / warehouse carve-out (a scope decision, not a gap):** a dbt warehouse (derived medallion
models, not a migration-owned schema) does **NOT** use tbls — its drift gate is **committed model
contracts (`models/**/_*.yml` + `tests:`) + CI `dbt parse`**. Don't bolt tbls onto a dbt repo (ktayl-data-platform).

> **HOW to do it → the `generate-schema-erd` skill** (the CI shape, per-toolchain migration-apply,
> the pin-everything rules that avoid false drift, the baseline recipe, the adopted/vendor-DB generator).
> Pulled on demand when a repo gains a schema — not restated here. Full gotcha history:
> memory `[[reference_tbls_erd_driftcheck]]`. Org doc: `insurance-platform/schema-erd-autogenerated`.

Related: `project-governance.md` (SA artefact #7), `documentation.md` (DoD doc gate), `testing.md`
(CI layers), `reusable-scripts.md`, `[[reference_tbls_erd_driftcheck]]`, `[[reference_cnpg_migration_playbook]]`.
